samples: This module reads version strings of the form "major.minor.patch" (for example 1.4.2) into a structured version value, rejecting input that doesn't have exactly three parts or has parts that aren't non-negative whole numbers, and it reports which of those two problems occurred. It also prints versions back as dotted text, compares them by major, then minor, then patch, and can pick the greatest version from a list (or nothing if the list is empty). It includes a compatibility check that treats a candidate as acceptable when it has the same major version and is not older than the required one, but it does not handle pre-release or build suffixes like "-beta" or "+build5".

This module reads version strings of the form "major.minor.patch" (for example 1.4.2) into a typed version value, and reports a specific error if the text doesn't have exactly three parts or if a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It can print versions back as text, compare them in the usual order (major, then minor, then patch), and check whether a candidate can stand in for a required version (same major, and not older). It can also pick the greatest version from a list, giving nothing for an empty list. It does not handle pre-release or build suffixes such as "-beta" or "+build5", and it needs no special permissions.

This module lets you turn text like "1.4.2" into a version value (major, minor, patch, all non-negative whole numbers), print it back in the same dotted form, and compare versions in the usual order of major, then minor, then patch. Parsing is strict: it ignores surrounding whitespace, and it reports a specific error when the text doesn't have exactly three parts or when a part isn't a valid non-negative number. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and at least as new as the required one) and a way to find the greatest version in a list, giving nothing for an empty list. It does not handle pre-release or build suffixes such as "-beta" or "+build5".

This module reads version strings of the form "major.minor.patch" (e.g. 1.4.2) into a structured version value, and returns a specific error if the text doesn't have exactly three parts or if a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It can print versions back as text, compare them in the usual order (major, then minor, then patch), find the greatest version in a list (or nothing if the list is empty), and check whether a candidate is compatible with a required version, meaning the same major version and not older. It handles only plain three-part versions, so pre-release and build suffixes like "-beta" or "+build5" are not supported and will be rejected as invalid.

This module reads plain "major.minor.patch" text (such as 1.4.2) into a version value, and it prints versions back in that form. It reports a specific error when the text doesn't have exactly three parts, or when a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It also compares versions by major, then minor, then patch, and offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the one required) plus a way to find the greatest version in a list, giving nothing for an empty list. It doesn't handle pre-release or build suffixes (like "-beta" or "+build5"), so it only suits simple three-number versions.
